#001

Airport to Seoul: two trains, one line

#001 · Getting around
Airport to Seoul: two trains, one line

The airport train (AREX) comes in two kinds. Express is nonstop, with a reserved seat. All-stop is cheaper and takes your transit card. Seoul Station to Terminal 1, adult fare: Express takes 43 minutes for 13,000 won. All-stop takes about 60 minutes for 4,750 won.

FRIEND TIPLots of luggage and staying near Seoul Station? Take Express. Going to Hongdae? All-stop is easier.
TrainTo Seoul StationAdult fare
Express (nonstop)43 min from T1 · 51 min from T213,000 won
All-stopabout 60 min from T14,750 won

Bus or taxi? The 2026 video below compares all three.

#002

That happy jingle means "transfer here"

#002 · Getting around
That happy jingle means "transfer here"

Hear a cheerful Korean tune on Seoul subway lines 1 to 8? You're at a transfer station. The tune is "Pungnyeon" (good harvest), based on an old folk song. Before 2009 riders heard bird calls, beeps and even Vivaldi.

FRIEND TIPHear it, then check the screen for your line color.
WhenTransfer sound
Before 2009Beeps and bird calls; Vivaldi on lines 5–8
2009"Eolssiguya" by Kim Baek-chan, the first Korean tune
2023"Pungnyeon" by Park Kyung-hoon, picked by a public vote
2026New arrangement with bamboo flutes and a fiddle

Why the 2026 remix? Riders said the old version got lost in train noise. The National Gugak Center picked instruments whose sound cuts through it: daegeum and sogeum (bamboo flutes), haegeum (a two-string fiddle) and yanggeum (a hammered dulcimer).

풍년이 왔네pungnyeoni watne · A good harvest has come! (the line the tune is built on)
📍 See on map
#003

Get a transit card first

#003 · Getting around
Get a transit card first

Buy a T-money card at a convenience store and top it up with cash. It works on subways and buses. Staying 1 to 7 days in Seoul? The Climate Card tourist pass gives unlimited rides from 5,000 won a day.

FRIEND TIPShort-term passes are charged on the day you use them.
  1. Go to any convenience store (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven) and ask for a T-money card.
  2. Top it up with cash at the counter.
  3. Tap it on the reader at subway gates and when you get on and off buses.
Climate Card tourist passPrice
1 day5,000 won
2 days8,000 won
3 days10,000 won
5 days15,000 won
7 days20,000 won

The physical card costs 3,000 won extra. Leaving Korea? You can ride the airport train and get off at Incheon Airport T1 or T2 with the pass, but you can't board there with it, so it won't cover your first ride into Seoul. It does not cover red express buses (gwangyeok) or GTX.

#004

Don't tip. Not even in a taxi.

#004 · Money
Don't tip. Not even in a taxi.

Korea has no tipping culture. Menu prices already include tax and service, and taxi drivers don't expect a tip either.

FRIEND TIPA warm "thank you" works better than a tip.
Seoul taxiWhat to know
Red 빈차 signEmpty. Wave it down.
Day base fare4,800 won (first 1.6 km)
Late night5,800 won (10–11 PM, 2–4 AM), 6,700 won (11 PM–2 AM)
PayingCard, T-money or cash. No tip.

Can't pronounce the address? Show the driver the place name in Korean on your map app.

#005

Your foreign card won't open the subway gate

#005 · Money
Your foreign card won't open the subway gate

Visa or Mastercard won't work at Seoul subway gates. Get a T-money or Climate Card first. You can buy them at stations or convenience stores.

FRIEND TIPSort out your transit card on day one. It makes everything easier.
  1. Buy a T-money card or a Climate Card at a station or convenience store.
  2. Top up a T-money card with cash.
  3. Tap the card on the gate. That's it.
#006

Side dishes are free, and so are refills

#006 · Eating
Side dishes are free, and so are refills

Those small dishes are called banchan. They come free with your meal. Usually you can ask for more, also free.

FRIEND TIPSome places have a self-serve banchan bar. Take only what you'll eat.
반찬 더 주세요banchan deo juseyo · More side dishes, please.
#007

Water is free, and often self-serve

#007 · Eating
Water is free, and often self-serve

Water or barley tea comes free at Korean restaurants. Many places have a self-serve water station with small cups.

FRIEND TIPDon't wait for a waiter to bring water. Look around for the cups.
물은 셀프mul-eun selpeu · A common sign: "Water is self-service."
#008

Shoes off at the door

#008 · Manners
Shoes off at the door

Take your shoes off before entering a Korean home. Some restaurants have floor seating, and you take shoes off there too.

FRIEND TIPSee shoes lined up at the entrance? Take yours off as well.
#009

The pink seat is for pregnant women

#009 · Manners
The pink seat is for pregnant women

Pink seats on the subway are kept for pregnant women. Leave them empty if you can.

FRIEND TIPNot sure? Just stand. Nobody minds.
#010

Call 1330 for travel help

#010 · Safety
Call 1330 for travel help

Lost or confused? Call 1330, the Korea Travel Hotline. It's free, run by the Korea Tourism Organization. Staff speak English, Japanese, Chinese and more.

FRIEND TIPFrom a foreign phone, dial +82-2-1330. You can also chat on KakaoTalk, WhatsApp or Line.
  1. Call 1330 from a Korean phone. From a foreign phone, call +82-2-1330.
  2. Or chat with them on KakaoTalk, WhatsApp, LINE or Facebook.
📞 Call 1330
#011

Convenience stores sell basic medicine

#011 · Safety
Convenience stores sell basic medicine

Sick at night? Convenience stores sell basic medicine. Think fever reducers, cold medicine, digestion aids and pain patches. For anything serious, see a pharmacy or call 119.

FRIEND TIPThe government plans to expand the list from 11 to 20 items. We'll update this when it happens.
FeelingLook forExample
Fever, headacheFever reducer / pain reliefTylenol (타이레놀)
ColdCold medicinePancol (판콜)
Upset stomachDigestion aidBearse (베아제)
Sore musclesPain patch—
감기약 주세요gamgiyak juseyo · Cold medicine, please.
#012

Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for walking

#012 · Phone & apps
Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for walking

Google Maps here shows transit, but not walking routes yet. Locals use Naver Map or KakaoMap. Naver Map has an English mode.

FRIEND TIPKorea approved Google's map data on Nov 13. Walking routes may come later.
AppBus & subwayWalking
Naver Map✓✓
KakaoMap✓✓
Google Maps✓✗ (not yet)
#014

"Gamsahamnida" — thank you

#014 · Say it in Korean
"Gamsahamnida" — thank you

If you learn one word, make it gamsahamnida (감사합니다). It means "thank you." Say it to drivers, staff, anyone.

FRIEND TIPShort version with friends: gomawo (고마워).
감사합니다gamsahamnida · Thank you.
#015

"Yeogiyo!" — excuse me, over here

#015 · Say it in Korean
"Yeogiyo!" — excuse me, over here

To get a server's attention, say "Yeogiyo" (여기요). It means "over here." Raising a hand works too.

FRIEND TIPSay it once, then wait. They'll come.
여기요yeogiyo · Excuse me! (to call staff)
#016

A big night view without the crowds

#016 · Hidden places
A big night view without the crowds

Skip the Namsan crowds. Yongmasan Skywalk shows Seoul's lights from the east. From Sagajeong Station (Line 7), walk about 50 minutes uphill.

FRIEND TIPIt closes on snowy or icy days.
📍 See on map
#017

Walk the old city wall at sunset

#017 · Hidden places
Walk the old city wall at sunset

Naksan Park sits beside Seoul's old city wall. Walk the wall trail at sunset for city lights. The park is free, and the trail is open 24 hours.

FRIEND TIPStation: Hyehwa, Line 4, Exit 2.
📍 See on map
#018

Winter in Seoul is truly cold

#018 · Seasons
Winter in Seoul is truly cold

Seoul winters are cold and dry. January averages about -2°C. Pack a warm coat, gloves and a hat.

FRIEND TIPConvenience stores sell hand warmers.
#019

Late June to July is rainy season

#019 · Seasons
Late June to July is rainy season

Rainy season, called jangma, usually runs from late June to late July. In central Korea it lasts about a month, with rain on roughly 18 of those days.

FRIEND TIPPack a small umbrella and shoes that can get wet.
#020

Why the 4th floor says "F"

#020 · Why is Korea like this?
Why the 4th floor says "F"

In some elevators, 4 becomes "F." In Korean, "four" sounds like the word for death. Some buildings skip it entirely.

FRIEND TIPMany hospitals skip the 4th floor altogether.
#021

Seoul bus numbers are a map

#021 · Getting around
Seoul bus numbers are a map

Bus colors tell you the distance: blue buses cross the city, green ones stay local, red ones go to nearby cities. On a blue bus, the first digit is the zone where it starts and the second is where it ends. Bus 506 runs from zone 5 to zone 0, downtown.

FRIEND TIPTap your card when you get off too, or you lose the transfer discount.
ZoneAreas (example)
0Jongno, Jung, Yongsan (downtown, Myeongdong)
1Dobong, Gangbuk, Seongbuk, Nowon
2Dongdaemun, Jungnang, Seongdong, Gwangjin
3Gangdong, Songpa (Jamsil)
4Seocho, Gangnam
5Dongjak, Gwanak, Geumcheon
6Gangseo, Yangcheon, Yeongdeungpo, Guro
7Eunpyeong, Seodaemun, Mapo (Hongdae)

Transfers: board your next bus or subway within 30 minutes of getting off (60 minutes from 9 PM to 7 AM) and you pay little or nothing extra, up to 4 transfers per trip.

Subway station numbers work the same way. Station 228 is the 28th stop on Line 2. Subtract two station numbers and multiply by about 2 for a rough travel time in minutes.

#022

Winter brings snacks you won't see in summer

#022 · Seasons
Winter brings snacks you won't see in summer

When it gets cold, street carts appear with three winter favorites: bungeoppang (fish-shaped bread with sweet red bean, no fish), hotteok (a pancake with melted brown sugar inside) and roasted sweet potatoes.

FRIEND TIPBite hotteok slowly. The sugar inside is very hot.
SnackWhat's inside
Bungeoppang 붕어빵Sweet red bean (sometimes custard). No fish.
Hotteok 호떡Brown sugar syrup, sometimes with seeds or nuts
Goguma 군고구마Just a sweet potato, roasted in a drum
이거 하나 주세요igeo hana juseyo · One of these, please.

Want to sit down while you eat? Gwangjang Market has rows of food stalls with benches.

#023

Ikseon-dong: 100-year-old houses, now cafés

#023 · Hidden places
Ikseon-dong: 100-year-old houses, now cafés

In September 2026, Time Out named Jongno 3-ga the coolest neighborhood in the world (it was 3rd in 2021). Its heart is Ikseon-dong, a maze of small hanok houses from the 1920s, now full of tiny cafés and shops.

FRIEND TIPGet off at Jongno 3-ga Station (Lines 1, 3, 5). At night, walk next door to Seosulla-gil along the Jongmyo wall.

Why so many small hanok here? In the 1920s, under Japanese rule, developer Jeong Se-kwon bought land downtown and built small, modern hanok with running water and indoor toilets, sold in installments, so Koreans could keep living in the old city. He built much of Bukchon too.

#024

The Han River's oldest bridge is 126 years old

#024 · Hidden places
The Han River's oldest bridge is 126 years old

Hangang Railway Bridge opened in 1900 as the first bridge across the Han, and trains still cross it. Hangang Bridge followed in 1917 as the first bridge for people. Today Seoul has more than 25 Han River bridges, and each has a story.

FRIEND TIPFor a sunset walk, cross Hangang Bridge to Nodeul Island.
BridgeFun fact
Hangang BridgeMore than 320 bullet marks from the Korean War were left in place.
Banpo BridgeGuinness record (2008) for the world's longest bridge fountain
Wonhyo BridgeWhere the monster lives in the film The Host (2006)
Mapo BridgeSeen in Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015)
Cheongdam BridgeThe only one you can't walk across
#025

Busan and Gyeongju work as day trips

#025 · Hidden places
Busan and Gyeongju work as day trips

The KTX bullet train gets you from Seoul Station to Busan in under 3 hours and to Gyeongju (Singyeongju Station) in about 2. Leave early and you can sleep in Seoul that night.

FRIEND TIPWeekend KTX seats sell out. Book a few days ahead on Korail's website.
WhereDon't miss
BusanTiny sky capsules gliding along the sea at Haeundae
GyeongjuGrassy hills downtown that are Silla royal tombs, about 1,500 years old

한국에 처음 온 친구에게 들려주고 싶은 101가지

외국인 친구가 방금 서울에 도착했다면, 꼭 해 주고 싶은 이야기를 하나씩 모았어요.

24/ 101개 공개
📍지도
최근 업데이트 2026.11.24 · 매주 새 이야기
글 배윤식 · 쉐어하우스 × 하우투서울

한국이 처음인 친구에게 가장 중요한 다섯 가지는 이렇습니다. 교통카드부터 사고, 걸을 땐 네이버지도나 카카오맵을 쓰고, 곤란하면 1330에 전화하고, 팁은 주지 않고, 밤에 아프면 편의점에서 기본 상비약을 살 수 있습니다.

30초만 있다면

이 다섯 가지만 기억하세요.

  1. #003
    교통카드부터 사세요단기권은 사용 당일에만 충전할 수 있어요.
  2. #012
    걸어갈 땐 네이버지도·카카오맵정부가 11월 13일 구글 지도 반출 요건 충족을 확인했어요. 도보 길찾기는 나중에 열릴 수 있어요.
  3. #010
    곤란할 땐 1330해외 번호 휴대폰이면 +82-2-1330. 카카오톡·왓츠앱·라인 채팅도 돼요.
  4. #004
    팁은 안 줘도 돼요. 택시도요팁보다 '감사합니다' 한마디가 더 통해요.
  5. #011
    밤에 아프면 편의점정부가 품목을 11개에서 20개로 늘리는 방안을 추진하고 있어요. 바뀌면 고칠게요.
📍
하우투서울 맵에서 장소 보기영상에 나온 12곳과 가까운 지하철역을 한눈에. 101 이야기 중 4개가 지도에 있어요.

서울 지하철 1~8호선에서 신나는 국악이 나오면 환승역이라는 뜻이에요. 지금 곡은 경기민요 '풍년가'를 바탕으로 한 '풍년'이에요. 2009년 전에는 새소리, 전자음, 비발디까지 나왔어요.

친구 팁음악이 들리면 화면에서 갈아탈 노선 색을 확인하세요.

#003 · 도착·교통
교통카드부터 사세요

편의점에서 티머니 카드를 사서 현금으로 충전하세요. 지하철·버스 모두 돼요. 서울에 1~7일 머문다면 기후동행카드 단기권(1일 5,000원부터)도 좋아요.

친구 팁단기권은 사용 당일에만 충전할 수 있어요.
  1. 편의점(CU·GS25·세븐일레븐)에서 티머니 카드를 달라고 하세요.
  2. 계산대에서 현금으로 충전해요.
  3. 지하철 개찰구와 버스 탈 때·내릴 때 단말기에 찍어요.

2일권8,000원
3일권10,000원

실물카드는 3,000원 따로예요. 출국할 때 공항철도를 타고 인천공항 T1·T2역에서 내리는 건 되지만, 인천공항역에서 타는 건 안 돼서 도착 첫날 서울로 갈 때는 못 써요. 광역버스·GTX도 안 돼요.

버스 색은 거리를 알려줘요. 파란 버스는 시내를 길게 가로지르고, 초록 버스는 동네를 돌고, 빨간 버스는 서울 밖 도시로 가요. 파란 버스 번호의 첫 숫자는 출발 권역, 둘째 숫자는 도착 권역이에요. 506번은 5권역에서 도심인 0권역으로 가요.

친구 팁내릴 때도 카드를 찍어야 환승 할인을 받아요.

1도봉·강북·성북·노원

환승: 내린 뒤 30분 안에(밤 9시~아침 7시는 60분) 다음 버스나 지하철을 타면 추가 요금이 거의 없어요. 한 번 이동에 최대 4번까지 돼요.

지하철 역 번호도 규칙이 있어요. 228은 2호선 28번째 역이에요. 두 역 번호를 빼고 2를 곱하면 대략 걸리는 시간(분)이 나와요.

#022

겨울에만 보이는 길거리 간식

#022 · 계절
겨울에만 보이는 길거리 간식

날이 추워지면 길거리 노점에 겨울 간식 3총사가 나타나요. 붕어빵(팥이 든 붕어 모양 빵, 붕어는 없어요), 호떡(속에 녹은 흑설탕), 군고구마예요.

친구 팁호떡은 천천히 드세요. 속의 설탕이 아주 뜨거워요.
간식속은?
붕어빵팥 (슈크림도 있어요). 붕어는 없어요.
호떡흑설탕 시럽, 씨앗·견과가 들어가기도 해요
군고구마드럼통에 구운 고구마 그대로
이거 하나 주세요igeo hana juseyo · 이거 하나 주세요.

앉아서 먹고 싶다면 광장시장에 의자 있는 먹거리 노점이 줄지어 있어요.

#023

익선동: 100년 된 한옥이 카페가 됐어요

#023 · 숨은 장소
익선동: 100년 된 한옥이 카페가 됐어요

2026년 9월 타임아웃이 종로3가를 '세계에서 가장 멋진 동네' 1위로 뽑았어요(2021년엔 3위). 그 중심이 1920년대 작은 한옥이 골목골목 모인 익선동이에요. 지금은 작은 카페와 가게로 가득해요.

친구 팁종로3가역(1·3·5호선)에서 내리세요. 밤에는 바로 옆 종묘 돌담길 서순라길을 걸어 보세요.

왜 여기 작은 한옥이 이렇게 많을까요? 일제강점기인 1920년대, 개발업자 정세권이 도심 땅을 사서 수도·전기와 실내 화장실을 갖춘 작은 한옥을 지어 나눠 갚는 방식으로 팔았어요. 조선 사람들이 도심에서 밀려나지 않게 하려던 거예요. 북촌 한옥 상당수도 그가 지었어요.

한강에서 가장 오래된 다리는 126살

#024 · 숨은 장소
한강에서 가장 오래된 다리는 126살

1900년에 놓인 한강철교가 한강 첫 다리예요. 지금도 기차가 다녀요. 사람이 건너는 첫 다리는 1917년 한강대교였어요. 지금 서울엔 한강 다리가 25개가 넘고, 다리마다 이야기가 있어요.

친구 팁노을 산책은 한강대교를 건너 노들섬까지 걸어 보세요.
다리알고 보면

부산·경주도 당일치기가 돼요

#025 · 숨은 장소
부산·경주도 당일치기가 돼요

친구 팁주말 KTX는 금방 매진돼요. 며칠 전에 코레일에서 예매하세요.

#001

Del aeropuerto a Seúl: dos trenes, una línea

#001 · Moverse
Del aeropuerto a Seúl: dos trenes, una línea

El tren del aeropuerto (AREX) tiene dos tipos. El Express es directo y con asiento reservado. El tren normal (All-stop) es más barato y se paga con tu tarjeta de transporte. De la estación de Seúl a la Terminal 1, tarifa de adulto: el Express tarda 43 minutos y cuesta 13,000 wones. El normal tarda unos 60 minutos y cuesta 4,750 wones.

CONSEJO DE AMIGO¿Mucho equipaje y te quedas cerca de la estación de Seúl? Toma el Express. ¿Vas a Hongdae? El tren normal es más fácil.

#002

Esa musiquita alegre significa "transbordo aquí"

#002 · Moverse
Esa musiquita alegre significa "transbordo aquí"

¿Escuchas una melodía coreana alegre en las líneas 1 a 8 del metro de Seúl? Estás en una estación de transbordo. Se llama "Pungnyeon" (buena cosecha) y viene de una canción popular antigua. Antes de 2009 sonaban pájaros, pitidos y hasta Vivaldi.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOCuando la escuches, mira la pantalla y busca el color de tu línea.
CuándoSonido de transbordo
Antes de 2009Pitidos y cantos de pájaros; Vivaldi en las líneas 5 a 8
2009"Eolssiguya" de Kim Baek-chan, la primera melodía coreana
2023"Pungnyeon" de Park Kyung-hoon, elegida por votación pública
2026Nuevo arreglo con flautas de bambú y un violín coreano

¿Por qué el nuevo arreglo de 2026? Los pasajeros decían que la versión anterior se perdía con el ruido del tren. El Centro Nacional de Gugak eligió instrumentos que se oyen por encima: daegeum y sogeum (flautas de bambú), haegeum (violín de dos cuerdas) y yanggeum (un salterio).

#003

Primero, consigue una tarjeta de transporte

#003 · Moverse
Primero, consigue una tarjeta de transporte

Compra una tarjeta T-money en una tienda de conveniencia y recárgala con efectivo. Sirve en metro y autobús. ¿Te quedas de 1 a 7 días en Seúl? El pase turístico Climate Card da viajes ilimitados desde 5,000 wones al día.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOLos pases cortos se cobran el día en que empiezas a usarlos.
  1. Ve a cualquier tienda de conveniencia (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven) y pide una tarjeta T-money.
  2. Recárgala con efectivo en la caja.
  3. Pásala por el lector en las puertas del metro y al subir y bajar del autobús.

La tarjeta física cuesta 3,000 wones aparte. ¿Te vas de Corea? Con el pase puedes bajar del tren del aeropuerto en Incheon T1 o T2, pero no subir allí, así que no sirve para tu primer viaje a Seúl. No sirve en los autobuses rojos (gwangyeok) ni en el GTX.

#004

No dejes propina. Ni en el taxi.

#004 · Dinero
No dejes propina. Ni en el taxi.

En Corea no hay cultura de propina. Los precios del menú ya incluyen impuestos y servicio, y los taxistas tampoco esperan propina.

Visa o Mastercard no funcionan en los torniquetes del metro de Seúl. Consigue primero una T-money o una Climate Card. Se venden en las estaciones y en tiendas de conveniencia.

#018

El invierno en Seúl es muy frío

#018 · Estaciones
El invierno en Seúl es muy frío

Los inviernos en Seúl son fríos y secos. En enero la temperatura promedio es de unos -2 °C. Lleva abrigo, guantes y gorro.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOEn las tiendas de conveniencia venden calentadores de manos.
#019

De fines de junio a julio es temporada de lluvias

#019 · Estaciones
De fines de junio a julio es temporada de lluvias

La temporada de lluvias, llamada jangma, suele ir de fines de junio a fines de julio. En el centro de Corea dura alrededor de un mes, con lluvia unos 18 de esos días.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOLleva un paraguas pequeño y zapatos que se puedan mojar.
#020

Por qué el piso 4 dice "F"

#020 · ¿Por qué Corea es así?
Por qué el piso 4 dice "F"

En algunos elevadores el 4 aparece como "F". En coreano, "cuatro" suena como la palabra "muerte". Algunos edificios ni siquiera tienen piso 4.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOMuchos hospitales se saltan el cuarto piso.
#021

Los números de autobús de Seúl son un mapa

#021 · Moverse

El color indica la distancia: los azules cruzan la ciudad, los verdes se quedan en el barrio y los rojos van a ciudades cercanas. En un autobús azul, el primer dígito es la zona donde empieza y el segundo, donde termina. El 506 va de la zona 5 a la zona 0, el centro.

#023

Ikseon-dong: casas de 100 años convertidas en cafés

#023 · Lugares escondidos
Ikseon-dong: casas de 100 años convertidas en cafés

En septiembre de 2026, Time Out nombró a Jongno 3-ga el barrio más cool del mundo (fue 3.º en 2021). Su corazón es Ikseon-dong, un laberinto de pequeñas casas hanok de los años 1920, hoy llenas de cafecitos y tiendas.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOBájate en la estación Jongno 3-ga (líneas 1, 3 y 5). De noche, camina al lado por Seosulla-gil, junto al muro de Jongmyo.

¿Por qué hay tantas hanok pequeñas aquí? En los años 1920, bajo el dominio japonés, el promotor Jeong Se-kwon compró terrenos en el centro y construyó hanok pequeñas y modernas, con agua corriente y baño interior, que vendía a plazos para que los coreanos pudieran seguir viviendo en la ciudad vieja. También construyó gran parte de Bukchon.

El puente más antiguo del río Han tiene 126 años

#024 · Lugares escondidos
El puente más antiguo del río Han tiene 126 años

El puente ferroviario Hangang abrió en 1900 como el primer puente sobre el Han, y los trenes todavía lo cruzan. El puente Hangang llegó en 1917 como el primero para personas. Hoy Seúl tiene más de 25 puentes sobre el Han, y cada uno tiene su historia.

CONSEJO DE AMIGOPara un paseo al atardecer, cruza el puente Hangang hasta la isla Nodeul.
